title: Profile-matched prefix-future contrast on synthetic payment histories
setting: Synthetic transaction histories (20 events: log-amount, log-gap, channel one-hot) where a hidden resource-usage trait drives channel switching and the fraud label; activity (amount/timing) is correlated with that trait by a tunable amount. A 32-unit GRU is optionally pretrained without labels on prefix-to-future-summary contrast (candidates profile-matched on activity, or random) plus activity-prediction and dispersion terms, then fully fine-tuned with class-balanced loss on a labeled fraction. The metric is average precision on 3000 fresh held-out users; recall and precision at a 0.5% review budget are diagnostics.

paper.title: TRIDENT-Seq: Profile-Matched Prefix-Future Contrast for Label-Efficient Payment Risk Modeling
paper.claim: Pretraining with prefix-future contrast over activity-profile-matched candidates improves risk ranking over scratch training and over random-candidate contrast, especially when labels are scarce.

metric.name: ap
metric.description: Average precision of the fine-tuned model's scores on 3000 held-out synthetic users (about 10% positives).

factors.name: method
factors.description: scratch: GRU trained only on labeled subset; pfc_matched: PFC pretraining with profile-matched candidates then fine-tune; pfc_random: same pretraining with all in-batch futures as candidates.

factors.name: label_frac
factors.description: Fraction of the 1200-user labeled pool used for fine-tuning.

factors.name: act_corr
factors.description: Correlation between hidden risk trait and activity level (amount/timing). 0 means activity is a pure confounder-free nuisance; 0.7 means activity is a strong proxy for risk.

factors.name: pretrain_domain
factors.description: Whether unlabeled pretraining histories come from the target generator or a shifted one (different channel preferences, amount/timing offsets, weaker risk-switching link).
